title: The Big Bang
seo_title: Big Bang Worksheets: Redshift, Hubble's Law and the Cosmic Microwave Background (Earth Science)
standard_text: Construct an explanation of the Big Bang theory based on astronomical evidence of light spectra, motion of distant galaxies, and composition of matter in the universe.
meta_desc: Free high school Earth and space science worksheets on the Big Bang (NGSS HS-ESS1-2): redshift, Hubble's law, galaxy data, the cosmic microwave background and hydrogen and helium. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Redshift, the CMB and hydrogen-helium amounts all support the Big Bang.
body_html:
How to think about it

The universe began hot and dense about 13.8 billion years ago and is still expanding.

  • Redshift: light from distant galaxies is stretched; farther galaxies recede faster (Hubble's law v = H₀d).
  • The cosmic microwave background is leftover glow from the early universe.
  • About 75% hydrogen and 25% helium matches Big Bang predictions; heavier elements came later from stars.
Example

Galaxy 200 Mpc away (H₀ = 70)?

70 × 200

Answer: 14,000 km/s

Example

Line 500 nm → 505 nm. z?

5 ÷ 500

Answer: 0.01

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the Big Bang exploded from one center in space.
  • Thinking redshift means the galaxy is hot.
  • Thinking nearby galaxies recede fastest.

faq.q: What is the evidence for the Big Bang?
faq.a: Redshifted light from distant galaxies (expansion), the cosmic microwave background, and the amounts of hydrogen and helium in the universe.
A galaxy's speed away from us is proportional to its distance: v = H₀d, with H₀ about 70 km/s per megaparsec.
When a light source moves away, its light is stretched to longer (redder) wavelengths.

items.q: Why is the CMB now in the microwave range?
c: The universe's expansion stretched the early light to much longer wavelengths.

items.q: What is redshift?
c: light from an object moving away is stretched to longer wavelengths

items.q: A spectral line at 400 nm in the lab is seen at 404 nm in a galaxy. What is the redshift z = Δλ ÷ λ?
Is the Big Bang an explosion into empty space from one center?
c: Yes, from the center of the universe.
No. Space itself expands everywhere at once.

items.q: Evidence: Almost every distant galaxy's light is redshifted. What does it support?
c: Space itself is stretching everywhere (Hubble's law).
This is leftover radiation from the hot early universe (the CMB).
The early universe was hot, dense and very uniform, then cooled as it expanded.
items.e: Three main lines of evidence: redshift, the CMB and light-element abundances.

items.q: What is the Big Bang theory?
c: The universe began about 13.8 billion years ago in a hot, dense state and has been expanding ever since.
Earth formed first, then the stars.
A star exploded in the middle of space.
The universe has always been the same.

items.q: Evidence: The farther a galaxy is, the faster it moves away. What does it support?
c: This is leftover radiation from the hot early universe (the CMB).
This matches what the Big Bang model predicts for the first few minutes.
Space itself is stretching everywhere (Hubble's law).
